text:
tara: Heads-up — noticed a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate (~35%) for prod-gpu-rt after the compile+kernel rollout this morning. Suspect eviction churn.
deploy-bot: kernel-rollout: prod-gpu-rt -> kernel-variant=v3.14 at 1923456820 :white_check_mark:
liam: Can you paste the short window metrics (hit-rate, evictions/sec, avg latency)?
tara: Sure — quick snippet from `cache-metrics` during the incident window:
```
2026-03-18T08:20Z hit_rate=0.62 -> 0.40
2026-03-18T08:20Z evictions_per_min=12 -> 78
2026-03-18T08:20Z avg_infer_latency_ms=42 -> 51
```
jason: That aligns with the quant-profile change we pushed to a subset of Llama-2 variants yesterday (aggressive fp8 path). Could be combo of kernel selection + different KV layout leading to key mismatch or inefficient locality.
maria: Also saw batching heuristic change in the last deploy — `max_batch_seq_threshold` bumped 8->12 in v3.14 which increases mixed-length batches. Mixed batches can change prefix alignment and reduce effective reuse.
liam: Two hypotheses: 1) cache key normalization/serialization changed (e.g., removed canonical whitespace/metadata), 2) eviction policy reacting to different seq-length distribution and kernel-induced latency variance.
tara: Ran a quick key diff from a sample of traces. Before vs after (first 3 keys):
```
BEFORE: a1f3c9... a1f3c9... (three duplicates)
AFTER: 9c4b2e... b7d9f0... c3a1d2... (more entropy)
```
tara: So we see >50% fewer duplicate prefix keys in the after traces.
liam: Can you confirm serialization version in runtime header? `X-Cache-Key-Version` or similar? If kernel swap changed serialization order (cat vs flatten) keys will diverge even if logical prefix identical.
tara: Header included `ckv=2` in both, but the runtime now sets `enable_rotary_alias`=true in v3.14. That flag toggles a code path that appends a binary fingerprint of attention tables to the cache key.
jason: Ah — we intentionally added that fingerprint to avoid invalid KVC across incompatible kernel/attn combos, but for mixed deployments it increases key cardinality and prevents sharing. We may have been too aggressive.
maria: :thinking: So it's working as intended for safety but kills sharing. What are quick mitigations?
liam: Options:
- revert `enable_rotary_alias` for prod until we can gate it by model ABI
- add a two-tier key: (logical-prefix-hash, detail-fingerprint) and let evictor prioritize logical-prefetch reuse
- pre-warm hot prefixes after rollout using sampled prefixes
- tune evictor hysteresis (increase TTL for recently used keys)

tara: I'll open a rollback PR for the flag and start a canary with the two-tier key idea behind a runtime flag. Can we also run a pre-warm job? @liam can you run `scripts/prefix_warmup.py --sample 100k` against canary?
liam: On it. Running now. Pushing warmup job to canary group at 1923459000. Link to job: https://internal-redwood/pipelines/1234 (perf dash will show impact). :rocket:
infra-bot: batch-warmup job scheduled: warmup-1923459000 for group canary-prod at 1923459000
jason: If we revert flag, watch for silent failcases where kernel expects the fingerprint. We should fallback to kernel-compatible variants, not NACK.
maria: Also lower batch timeout to reduce mixing - from 50ms -> 30ms for canary to test effect on hit-rate without full revert.
tara: Action items summarized:
- tara: open rollback PR for `enable_rotary_alias` on prod-gpu-rt
- liam: run prefix warmup + post-warmup hit-rate report (job 1234)
- jason: prototype two-tier key implementation behind feature flag
- maria: adjust batch timeout on canary to 30ms and monitor cost delta
Monitoring knobs: hit_rate, evictions_per_min, avg_latency, tokens/sec. Alert if hit_rate < 0.55 for >5m. @everyone :eyes:
liam: Will report back in ~30m with numbers.
tara: Thanks — this explains the eviction oscillation pattern. We'll avoid full revert until canary data arrives. :thumbsup:
